Self-QA walkthrough of the CBI pilot in Add Entity modal (Business Interruption -> contingent BI), simulated step-by-step in code since no browser automation tool was available this session. Found 4 issues, ranked by severity:

1. RACE CONDITION (real, not theoretical): mock-config.ts's default scenario has delayMs:300. The third-party search box (onThirdPartyQueryChange) fires a new async MockThirdPartyService.search() call on every keystroke with no debounce and no request-sequencing guard. Typing a normal query overlaps multiple 300ms-delayed calls; an older response can resolve after a newer one and overwrite thirdPartyResults with stale data. This exact bug class already has an established fix pattern in this codebase (TrackerService's ticketsRequestSeq/ticketRequestSeq counters) that wasn't applied here.
2. NO ERROR HANDLING: mock-config.ts's 'flaky' scenario (errorRate 0.3) makes MockThirdPartyService.search() throw. onThirdPartyQueryChange does a bare await firstValueFrom(...) with no try/catch -> unhandled rejection, zero user-facing feedback, results just never update.
3. NO LOADING INDICATOR: with a 300ms delay per keystroke, there's no spinner or "Searching..." state, unlike every other search UI in this app (e.g. broker-search-modal's state$ + spinner pattern).
4. STICKY STATE (lower severity): switching Damage type away from Business Interruption and back leaves the contingent-BI checkbox, cbiCaseType, and selectedThirdParty signal exactly as they were -- none of it resets. This matches the app's existing behavior for the plain BI interruption dates (also never reset on damage-type change), so it's an extension of a pre-existing pattern rather than a new inconsistency, but third-party identity is higher-stakes data than a date and may be worth reconsidering.

Not fixed yet -- reporting per instruction to track findings before changing anything further.

Fixed all 4 self-QA findings from the previous note, same session:
1. Race condition -> replaced the manual async call with a debounceTime(250) + switchMap pipeline fed into toSignal() (mirrors broker-search-modal's searchTrigger$ pattern already in this codebase). switchMap cancels any in-flight search the instant a newer query comes in, so the 300ms default-scenario delay can no longer land out of order.
2. No error handling -> catchError in the pipeline sets a thirdPartySearchError signal; template shows "Search failed. Try again." instead of silently doing nothing.
3. No loading indicator -> added an nx-spinner (swaps in for the search icon) while thirdPartySearching() is true, matching the app's other search modals.
4. Sticky CBI state -> the existing damage-type-change effect() now calls resetCbiState() whenever damageType is not business-interruption, clearing the checkbox, case type, third-party source/name/relationship, and any selected/searched third party.

Built a pilot, not a finished feature -- key finding first: "Claim Rejected" was ALREADY a selectable closure reason in the existing Close Claim flow (claim-closure-modal.component.ts:36) before this session touched anything. So "can a claim be rejected at all" was already answered; what was actually missing were the 3 things the real Confluence ticket calls out as unresolved:

1. Liability-related rejections needing a "waiting for underwriter" state before finalising -- built: a checkbox on the reason step ("This rejection involves a liability determination...") that only appears when reason = Claim Rejected. Checking it routes the claim to a new status, 'Pending Rejection Approval', instead of closing it immediately.
2. What happens while pending -- built: a warning banner + "Approve rejection" / "Decline rejection" buttons render directly on Claim Overview when status is Pending Rejection Approval. Approve runs the real closeClaim() flow with reason Claim Rejected (closes for real); Decline reverts status to Open.
3. Second-level approver notification (in-app queue vs email, who approves) -- NOT built. No auth/role system exists anywhere in this prototype (confirmed during earlier audit of BMPCC-13725/14869), so there's no real user to gate the Approve/Decline buttons behind -- they render for whoever is looking, same as every other role-agnostic action here. This is the honest gap; a real answer needs product/BA input on the actual approval routing before it can be built properly (maybe via the existing /approvals page, but that page's data model -- UrgentApproval -- is reserve/payment-shaped and doesn't fit a claim rejection without its own redesign).

Also NOT resolved: whether "Reject Claim" should be its own dedicated button (as the ticket's title implies) rather than a reason inside the generic Close Claim flow -- left as-is since changing that is a bigger UX call, not something to guess at.

Self-QA: walked every card on Claim Overview as a claims handler would (no browser tool -- code-traced every click path), specifically re-checking my own Pending Rejection Approval work. Found and fixed 4 real issues:

1. Missing space in the Policy field markup (unrelated to rejection, found along the way) -- "{{ claim.policyNumber }}@if(...)" rendered with no space before "(v2)". Fixed.
2. approveRejection()/declineRejection() had no error handling and no double-click guard -- a flaky-scenario failure would silently do nothing, and two fast clicks could fire closeClaim() twice. Added a rejectionActionInFlight signal (disables both buttons + spinner on Approve) and a try/catch with a toast.error() on failure.
3. The new 'Pending Rejection Approval' status fell through to StatusChipComponent's generic fallback (grey, same as Closed) -- a handler glancing at the chip couldn't tell a pending-approval claim from an actually-closed one. Added a real token mapping (reuses task-status-pending, the same amber token other domains already use for "awaiting action").
4. "Edit claim details" was still clickable while a rejection is pending underwriter review -- editing loss info mid-review could invalidate the basis of the decision. Now hidden alongside Closed.

Deliberately NOT changed (judgment calls, not bugs): left "Reassign handler" and the Recovery Potential card's own set/update action available during Pending Rejection Approval -- neither touches the rejection determination itself, blocking them felt like overreach rather than a clear fix.

Also surfaced but NOT fixed (pre-existing, unrelated to this session's work, flagging per the walkthrough instruction to check everything): several dead links/buttons found in adjacent cards that were never wired to anything -- "Start investigation" and the risk-score refresh icon (General Info row 2), "Loss event ID" (styled as a link, no click handler), and on Pending Tasks widget: "More options" (ellipsis), per-row "See details", and the 3 column sort-header chevrons. Cross-checked against the real production repo (github.developer.allianz.io/commercial-claims/claims-management, downloaded ZIP of main, 2026-08-31). Result: the entire CBI pilot has ZERO trace in real code. Grepped the whole real frontend (frontend/apps + frontend/libs) for "contingent", "CBI", "instructionStatus", "interruption" -- no hits except the literal string "Business Interruption" used as a plain damage-type label (damage-details-view-type.model.ts). Real entities-damages model (entities.model.ts) has no isContingentBi/cbiCaseType/thirdPartyName/instructionStatus/interruptionStartDate fields at all.

Bigger structural finding: real system does NOT split PD and BI into separate ClaimSection-style objects the way this prototype's core model assumes ("a section IS an entity x damage-type pairing"). Real treats BI as a view-type variant inside the same generic damage-capture flow (DamageDetailsViewType.FinancialLoss), not a structurally separate coverage object. This means the prototype's foundational assumption for where CBI would even attach may not hold.

This was always flagged as a pilot with no real Jira/AIP field list to build against -- this confirms it precisely: 100% invented, not a partial-spec gap-fill. Needs product/BA input on whether CBI is even modeled this way in the real target architecture before more work here is worthwhile.
